name: West Ridge / Southwest Face

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek Trail Trailhead (climbers' access near Upper Group Campground)
waypoints.directions: Park at the Goodell Creek Group Campground on SR-20 near Newhalem, at about 600 feet. The climbers' path begins behind a large boulder at the back of the Upper Group Campground. If you'll be camping in Terror Basin, North Cascades National Park requires a backcountry camping permit — pick it up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center (walk-up only, no advance reservations for this zone).

waypoints.name: Cairn / Terror Basin Route split
waypoints.note: Cairn marks where the climbers' path leaves the old logging roadbed and angles south of Terror Creek, climbing steeply toward treeline.

waypoints.name: Terror Basin Camp
waypoints.note: Gravelly, wildflower-covered basin with established tent sites and running snowmelt streams — the standard high camp shared by parties climbing any of the McMillan Spires.

waypoints.name: Basin notch above camp
waypoints.note: Notch just above camp gives a view down to Lake Azure and the glaciated cliffs below; from here the route crosses basin slabs and snow benches toward the East-West McMillan col.

waypoints.name: Snow gully below East-West McMillan col
waypoints.note: Steep snow/scree gully estimated in the 40-degree range on the approach to the col — crampons and axe essential; this is also the descent line, so watch for rockfall and parties below.

waypoints.name: East-West McMillan Col
waypoints.note: Crux decision point where the steep snow gully and the 4th-class rock ledge variant both top out before the final scramble to the East summit block.

itinerary.cal: Best conditions are July-September; North Cascades National Park requires a backcountry camping permit for Terror Basin (walk-up only, issued in person at Marblemount), and early-season parties should expect more glacier/snow travel and possibly a rope for crevasse hazard on the Terror Glacier approach.

days.note: Trailless approach from the Upper Goodell Creek trailhead: flat brushy trail for ~4 miles, then a steep, unmaintained climber's path gains ~4,000 ft up a forested ridge to heather benches, then descends slightly into Terror Basin. No water or reliable trail markers on the upper section — cairns and flagging only.
days.title: Approach to Terror Basin high camp

schedule.label: Leave Goodell Creek trailhead
schedule.detail: ~600 ft elevation, flat trail for first 4 miles

schedule.label: Start steep climber's path
schedule.detail: Gains ~4,000 ft up a forested ridge to ~3,200-4,000 ft benches

schedule.label: Arrive Terror Basin camp
schedule.detail: Gravelly flat basin at ~5,800 ft with running water and flowers

days.objective: Establish camp in Terror Basin (~5,800 ft)

days.note: From camp, cross benches to the outlet of the glacial lake, then climb snow/slabs and the Terror Glacier to West McMillan Spire's west ridge and summit (~8,000 ft). From there, downclimb and traverse the low-5th-class connecting ridge east to East McMillan Spire (7,992 ft), including a short rappel, then reverse the whole traverse back to West McMillan and down to camp. This is the long day of the trip — expect 10-14 hours camp to camp when both summits are combined.
days.title: West McMillan Spire, then traverse to East McMillan Spire

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start for glacier/snow travel while firm

schedule.label: Reach glacial lake outlet (~5,550 ft)
schedule.detail: Traverse benches, then rock and snow toward Terror Glacier

schedule.label: Summit West McMillan Spire (~8,000 ft)
schedule.detail: Via west ridge slabs above the glacier

schedule.label: Traverse connecting ridge to East McMillan Spire
schedule.detail: Low 5th-class climbing with a short rappel; tag the 7,992 ft summit

schedule.label: Back at West McMillan / descending
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge traverse and downclimb to the glacier

schedule.label: Return to Terror Basin camp
schedule.detail: Full round trip typically 10-14 hrs from camp

days.objective: Tag both McMillan summits via the connecting ridge

days.note: Break camp and reverse the Day 1 approach: climb back out of Terror Basin to the heather benches, then descend the steep forested ridge and flat trail to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip: ~7 mi and 5,700+ ft to a Terror Basin high camp, a long 10-14 hr summit day tagging both West and East McMillan Spire via the connecting ridge (with a short rappel), and a 7-mile hike out.

beta: Most parties climb East McMillan Spire as an add-on to West McMillan Spire via the shared Terror Basin/West Ridge approach, then traverse east along the connecting ridge crest (roughly 5.6) to tag the lower, eastern summit.
